attempts.prompt:
Korean webtoon panel, digitally inked and coloured by a professional webtoon studio. Crisp black ink with tapered strokes, heavier on the outer silhouette, the jaw, the hair mass and where forms overlap. Flat local colour with one hard-edged cool cel shadow per material. One named key light: its colour washes smoothly over the lit side. If the scene names a back light, it draws a thin crisp rim along the figure's silhouette. Everything else stays flat. Muted cool base palette of slate, navy and grey-blue, so the light source and the character's signature colour carry the saturation. Background simplified and lower in contrast than the characters. Small crisp highlights; glossy specular only on metal and wet surfaces.

Hand-made webtoon colouring: each garment has only a few large, opaque, clean-edged shadow shapes, placed in its real folds; no scattered translucent streaks, zigzag shards or crumpled-foil folds. Worn cloth shows a few small frayed notches and loose threads, never sawtooth edges along every edge. Plain shoes and clothes with no logos, stripes or brand marks. Every strap, buckle, pocket and seam is attached and has a purpose; no stray stitch marks. Matte skin, hair and stone; no 3D, low-poly or plastic look.

Establish recipe. A single full wide landscape panel, 1536 by 1024 pixels, aspect ratio 3:2. High camera with a wide lens. The location's cold white LED key lights are visible, with a full value range and small mid-value figures; calm at the top. No panel borders or inset images.

CHAPTER 1 P09: REDRAW THE SUBWAY PIT AT CORRECT SCALE. Use the attached approved site key ONLY for the location design, materials, cold night palette, tent/van types and gate position. Deliberately change its camera and scales to meet the dimensions below. This is a vast deep excavation with tiny people, viewed steeply from above, NOT a medium shot of hunters.
Camera: mounted about 4 metres above street level at the near street edge, angled steeply DOWN into the pit, about 55 degrees below horizontal. The pit floor is 22 metres below the camera. The horizon and any vanishing horizon line lie ABOVE the picture. See the TOPS of heads, shoulders, tent roof and van roof; bodies below are foreshortened toward the feet. All pit-wall vertical piles converge coherently downward, with ONE camera and ONE ground geometry. Keep all architecture and people in the same perspective. The far wall is visibly enormous, not a shallow hole.
The rectangular cut-and-cover subway pit is 18 metres deep, about ten human heights, roughly 25 metres across. It dominates the frame. Steel pile walls with timber boards, scaffold stairs descending the NEAR wall, blue tarps, wet concrete, puddles, yellow-and-black barriers. Scaffold stairs have NINE 2-metre rises, with a clear landing every 2 metres and 1.1-metre guard rails. Each 2-metre landing-to-landing rise is slightly greater than a standing adult height; NOT two tiny stair flights smaller than a person. Exactly two heavy cross-struts span the pit HIGH UP, with ample visible depth beneath them. Cold white LED floodlights on 8-metre poles at street level cast long crisp cool shadows and wet metal highlights. No golden lighting.
At the TOP LEFT of the frame, on the SAME street-level platform, the Association pop-up tent is 3 metres to the peak and the black Black Hound van is 2 metres high. Both are visibly higher than the 1.78-metre Jaeha standing BESIDE them, not behind at another depth. Jaeha is small in the frame, seen steeply from ABOVE AND BEHIND, with the crown of his head, rounded shoulders and orange vest visible. His back carries the one T patch; his face is not visible. Both arms hug ONE battered notebook tightly to his chest, no second notebook in the pocket. He stands planted on the street at the pit edge beside the tent, WELL SHORT of its roof and below the van roof. Do not enlarge him for emphasis. Guard rail meets his waist, never his knees. His underlying anatomy is 7.5-8 heads, long legs, with correct top-down foreshortening.
At the BOTTOM of the excavation near the FAR WALL are EXACTLY SEVEN TINY Black Hound hunters, matching the attached approved seven-person lineup, in TWO loose staggered clusters, one of three and one of four, never an eye-level lineup. Each is about 1.7-1.9 metres tall, roughly ONE TENTH of the 18-metre pit wall, with 7.5-8-head underlying anatomy. Their tiny heads and shoulders are seen from ABOVE. Only broad costume/hair/weapon silhouettes read; their faces are too small to read. One stretches, one laughs to a companion, one checks a weapon. Their feet are grounded at staggered depths. The seven silhouettes are spearman, bearded axe fighter, ponytail sword-and-buckler fighter, broad Mok with tower shield, male short-staff mage, black-bob crossbow woman and bald shield-bearer. Attached props must be held, slung or resting on the ground.
The gate is at the far wall on the BOTTOM floor between steel struts: a simple door-height black-violet slit with a PALE cold white-cyan rim, 2 metres high, only a little taller than those tiny hunters. The bottom has NO tent, no van and no oversized people. The tent and van are ONLY at street level at top left.
Leave the top band calm and low in contrast for the location tag: simple dark navy city/night shapes with no letters. Keep one readable focal path from the orange speck at street level down the scaffold tower to the tiny hunters and slit far below. Full model-sheet proportions, no compressed bodies; crop at the frame edge instead. No readable faces in this establishing shot. Everything must look hand-inked, crisp and flat cel-coloured as the acting anchor, rather than a 3D construction render.
